subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What happens to particles when a substance boils?
options: They gain energy and spread far apart as a gas
questions.explain: Boiling gives particles enough energy to overcome forces and move freely apart as a gas.

questions.q: In diamond, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to how many other carbons?
questions.explain: Each carbon in diamond forms four strong covalent bonds, giving a rigid giant structure.

questions.q: When do ionic compounds conduct electricity?
options: When molten or dissolved in water
questions.explain: Ions are only free to move and carry charge when the compound is molten or in solution.

questions.q: A covalent bond is formed when atoms:
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form when non-metal atoms share pairs of electrons.

questions.q: Which technique would best separate a soluble solid from its solution to obtain crystals?
questions.explain: Crystallisation evaporates the solvent so the dissolved solid forms crystals.

questions.q: Copper ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Copper ions give a green flame colour.

questions.q: Polymers are made of:
options: Many small molecules (monomers) joined into long chains
questions.explain: Polymers are long chains formed by joining many small monomer molecules.

questions.q: What happens to particles when a liquid freezes into a solid?
options: They gain energy and move apart
They lose energy and become fixed in a regular arrangement
questions.explain: On freezing, particles lose energy and settle into fixed positions in a regular pattern.

questions.q: Why is diamond unable to conduct electricity?
options: Its layers slide over each other
It has no charged particles free to move
questions.explain: In diamond every electron is held in a covalent bond, so none are free to carry charge.

questions.q: What is one advantage of instrumental methods such as flame emission spectroscopy?
options: They are fast, accurate and use very small samples
questions.explain: Instrumental methods like flame emission spectroscopy are fast, accurate and sensitive, working on tiny samples.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is identified because it:
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

questions.q: When sodium hydroxide is added to a solution of copper(II) ions, the precipitate is:
questions.explain: Copper(II) ions form a blue precipitate of copper hydroxide with sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: In ionic bonding, electrons are:
questions.explain: Electrons are transferred from the metal atom to the non-metal atom, forming ions.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: They are made of free electrons
Strong electrostatic forces throughout a giant lattice
questions.explain: Strong electrostatic attractions in the giant ionic lattice need lots of energy to break.

questions.q: When silver nitrate is added to a bromide solution, the precipitate formed is:
questions.explain: Bromide ions form a cream precipitate of silver bromide.

questions.q: Flame emission spectroscopy works by measuring the:
options: Light given out when metal ions are heated in a flame
questions.explain: In flame emission spectroscopy, heated metal ions emit light with a pattern that identifies them.

questions.q: How many covalent bonds are there in a molecule of methane, CH4?
questions.explain: Carbon forms four single covalent bonds, one to each hydrogen.

questions.q: Ionic bonding occurs between:
questions.explain: Ionic bonds form when a metal transfers electrons to a non-metal.

questions.q: A pure substance, unlike a mixture, will:
options: Melt and boil at specific sharp temperatures
Melt over a range of temperatures
questions.explain: A pure substance has a sharp, specific melting and boiling point, whereas mixtures melt and boil over a range.

questions.q: Oxygen gas can be identified because it:
questions.explain: Oxygen relights a glowing splint.

questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points?
questions.explain: Only weak intermolecular forces need to be overcome, not the strong covalent bonds.

questions.q: Silicon dioxide is an example of a:
questions.explain: Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.
